title: Ranch Sky
subtitle: Wilson family ranch, Sapaque / Waller Creek, Monterey County, CA, 1919-2026
label: Wilson family ranch
location_lines: NE1/4 SW1/4 Sec 17, T24S R8E, Mount Diablo Meridian
Monterey County, CA, Burnett Peak 7.5' quad
North side of the Waller Creek drainage; about 150 m outside the present Fort Hunter Liggett boundary
intro: 1771: Mission San Antonio de Padua founded in Salinan territory.
1839-45: Mexican ranchos granted nearby: El Piojo, Los Ojitos, San Miguelito de Trinidad, Pleyto, Milpitas.
1880: Ray, Harris and Liddle families farming Sapaque Valley.
1887: Bryson PO opens. Same year, gold is found in the Los Burros district (Last Chance mine).
1913 and 1942: big fires cross the pin.
1926: Lewis H. Smith patents the SW1/4 of Sec 17, which includes the pin.
1940-41: Army buys ~267,000 ac to form Hunter Liggett.
To 1941: Botts and Bryson quicksilver mines produce mercury 1.4-2.3 km NW.
owners: Mission San Antonio de Padua sphere
Not in any confirmed Mexican rancho; probably public land
US public land; the pin (NESW Sec 17) was unpatented until 1926. Lewis H. Smith's homestead claim was probably pending: he got the adjacent SE1/4 in 1920.
patent dates: BLM GLO; pending claim is an inference
Lewis H. Smith: patent SER-979910, Sec 17 SW1/4 incl. the pin
unknown (needs county deed research). Hunter Liggett (1941) took adjacent land; the pin parcel apparently stayed outside.
owners_note: Owners are shown only where a cited source supports them. Everything else says unknown.
homesteaders: Three generations of the Stanley family homesteaded just south of the pin and are buried at Pleyto Cemetery, which was relocated when Lake San Antonio flooded old Pleyto.
The last homesteaders next to the pin, the Russells (1931), were a father and son; the son became a noted token-and-medal numismatist.
Full notes with sources and confidence levels are in homesteaders.md.

slides.source: USGS Historical Topographic Map Collection - Bryson 15' (1:62,500)
slides.caption: Earliest map: Waller Creek and the South Fork drawn through section 17; no roads or buildings shown at the pin. ~6 km square.
slides.owner: US public land; Lewis H. Smith's homestead claim probably pending (he got the adjacent SE1/4 in 1920 and the pin's SW1/4 in 1926; the pending claim is an inference)
facts: Waller Creek and its South Fork are already named.
"Quicksilver Mine" is printed on Sycamore Creek about 1.4 km NW: today's Botts mercury mine.
Bryson post office (opened 1887; the area was once called Sapaque) was ~5 km SE.
The "Smith's Ranch" label on this sheet may be Lewis H. Smith's place (inference, not confirmed).

slides.source: USGS Historical Topographic Map Collection - Burnett Peak & Bryson 7.5' (1:24,000)
slides.caption: First detailed map: pin on Waller Creek drainage just SE of the 1202 ft knob, beside the Hunter Liggett Military Reservation boundary. No buildings or roads at the pin. ~3 km square.
slides.owner: after Lewis H. Smith's 1926 patent; later owners unknown
facts: The new Hunter Liggett Military Reservation boundary (1941) is drawn right beside the pin.
No roads or buildings are mapped at the pin yet.
The Sam Jones fire (35,455 ac) swept this ground in July 1953.

slides.source: USGS Historical Topographic Map Collection - Bryson 15' (1:62,500)

facts: Beartrap Road, Bald Mountain (2.3 km N) and Smith Ranch appear.

The 1953 Sam Jones fire had burned over this ground.
